solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Absorbed in enchanting show

definitions.meaning: a material that has drawn up moisture, as a lamp's wick does, has been soaked or taken in
a stage musical about the witches of Oz, so a show full of enchantment

explanation.surface: Someone is utterly captivated by a magical theatre production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absorbed' reads as 'engrossed', but it is the verb of a wick drawing up liquid; the second definition is the musical about the Wicked Witch of the West.
explanation.definitionFit: A wick soaks up liquid, so the past tense of that verb means soaked up; the second sense names a hit Broadway musical.

clue.text: Be vigilant — this could make synchronisation difficult!

definitions.meaning: a timepiece that is out of step would leave people unable to synchronise their watches

explanation.surface: A warning to stay alert, with a joke about clocks that disagree.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an alert to take care; read literally it describes a timepiece that is out, i.e. wrong.

clue.text: Left out of coterie, she's into 20

indicators.note: out of tells us the letter for left is taken away from the word for a coterie

parts.note: a coterie is a close social group, a circle

explanation.surface: A woman excluded from a social clique turns to witchcraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is WITCHCRAFT, so 'she's into 20' is a witch; Circe is the enchantress of the Odyssey who turned Odysseus's men into pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: Circe is the sorceress of Greek myth, so she is a woman devoted to the magic of 20-across.

clue.text: Reptile showing up in midst of the herd? Here's a way to show off your muscles!

definitions.text: Here's a way to show off your muscles!

indicators.note: in places the turned reptile inside the letters drawn from the herd

parts.note: the letters at the heart of the phrase the herd, spanning the gap between the two words, are E, H, E

indicators.note: showing up in a down clue means the reptile's name is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a croc, short for crocodile, is a reptile

explanation.surface: A crocodile surfaces among cattle, and then a boast about displaying muscles.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'midst of the herd' is EHE, from thE HErd; 'showing up' turns CROC into CORC, which goes 'in' it. An écorché is an artist's figure drawn or modelled with the skin removed.
explanation.definitionFit: This anatomical model, French for 'flayed', shows the body's musculature with no skin over it.

clue.text: Hellenic gatherings in the past attracting artists

indicators.note: attracting means the artists are drawn alongside, joined on after the past

parts.note: in the past is ago, as in 'long ago'
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist; RAS is the plural

explanation.surface: Ancient Greek assemblies drew in painters long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: An agora was the public assembly or marketplace of an ancient Greek city, so these are Greek meetings.

clue.text: See 15
Remember short skirts? Take a look outside — one about to go!

indicators.note: outside puts the word for taking a look around the short skirts
to go means one letter for about is dropped from the reconnaissance word

parts.note: a recce is a reconnaissance, a look round
one about is a single C, short for circa, Latin for about
minis are miniskirts, short skirts

explanation.surface: Someone nostalgically recalls the miniskirt era and urges a glance around.
explanation.walkthrough: RECCE loses one of its C's ('one about to go') to give RECE, which goes 'outside' MINIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To reminisce is to recall the past fondly, so it is a verb of memory like the clue's.

clue.text: Jenny's ashes scattered on surface of sea

indicators.note: scattered tells us the letters of ashes are strewn into a new order
surface of takes the top letter, the first, of sea

explanation.surface: Someone named Jenny has their cremated remains strewn over the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jenny' looks like a woman's name, but a jenny is a female donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A jenny is a female donkey, which is what a hyphenated she-ass also names.

clue.text: Initiate Sharp into MS Office — no peripherals required!

indicators.note: into places the sharp word inside what is left of the software name
computer peripherals are mice, so the letters of mice are removed from MS Office

parts.note: sharp in taste is tart

explanation.surface: An instruction to load a sharp program into Microsoft Office, without extra hardware.
explanation.walkthrough: The peripherals are MICE: M at the front and ICE at the back of MS OFFICE go, leaving SOFF, with TART put 'into' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To initiate something is to begin it, the phrasal-verb sense of getting things going.

clue.text: Leaving old city, resentment shown among fans in upset for Bavarians

indicators.note: among puts the trimmed resentment inside the jumbled fans in
upset means the letters of fans in are knocked into a new order
Leaving tells us the old city departs from the word for resentment

parts.note: rancour is bitter resentment
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city, crossword's favourite old city

explanation.surface: Bitterness breaks out in a crowd of upset supporters as they leave an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: RANCOUR 'Leaving' UR gives RANCO, set 'among' an anagram of FANS IN ('upset').
explanation.definitionFit: Franconia is a region of northern Bavaria in Germany, so its people are Bavarians.

clue.text: Band section given leave …

parts.note: an arm is a section or branch of an organisation
to let is to leave or allow, as in 'let it be'

explanation.surface: Part of a musical group is given time off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a musical group; it is a strip of material worn round the arm.
explanation.definitionFit: An armlet is a bracelet or ring of cloth worn around the upper arm.

clue.text: … to get rid of vocal in Oxford, for instance

indicators.note: vocal says the word for getting rid of is spoken out, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to shoo is to drive away, get rid of

explanation.surface: The ellipsis continues 10: a band given leave to shed a singer in Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' looks like the city, but an oxford is a lace-up shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxford is a style of laced leather footwear, so it is one example of the answer.

clue.text: In rough condition, Grace sings remarkably

indicators.note: remarkably suggests the letters of Grace sings are arranged in an unusual way

explanation.surface: Grace sings astonishingly well despite being in poor shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Cragginess is the quality of being rugged and rocky, a rough state of a landscape or face.

clue.text: Programming system involving many breakthroughs?

parts.note: early computers were programmed with cards punched full of holes, so the many breakthroughs are literal holes

explanation.surface: An innovative coding approach full of advances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breakthroughs' reads as scientific advances, but the holes punched through the cards are the breakthroughs.
explanation.definitionFit: Early computing took programs and data from stiff paper with holes knocked through it.

clue.text: On the way to a 21 Across?

definitions.text: On the way to a 21 Across?

parts.words: On the way to a 21 Across?
parts.note: 21 Across is ACME, a peak; a musical build-up rising in volume is heading for a climax

explanation.surface: A question about travelling towards a summit.
explanation.walkthrough: A crescendo is properly the build-up rather than the peak itself, so it is 'on the way to' the climax.
explanation.definitionFit: In music this marks a gradual increase in loudness, a rise that leads towards a peak.

clue.text: She's into 20, that girl, enraging me or surprising

parts.note: that girl is her

indicators.note: surprising suggests the letters of enraging me or are turned into an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A girl dabbling in witchcraft, angering someone in a startling way.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is WITCHCRAFT; the answer spans 15 and 5 down and names the witch from the Harry Potter books.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the clever young witch, Harry Potter's friend, studying magic at Hogwarts.

clue.text: Every second, still more stupefied by newspaper boss

parts.note: even is still, as in 'even better'
number is more numb, the comparative of a word for stupefied
ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Every moment someone is more dazed by their newspaper editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Every second' looks like time ticking by; it means every second item in a sequence, i.e. 2, 4, 6...
explanation.definitionFit: Taking every other item from one counted list leaves just those divisible by two.

clue.text: Put straightforwardly, this is new in cake

indicators.note: in places the letter for new inside the cake

parts.note: an éclair is a cream-filled choux cake

explanation.surface: Stated plainly, this is a fresh ingredient in a pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: French for 'in clear', it describes a message sent plainly rather than in code.

clue.text: 'From the South' — seen it, a meticulously abridged performance

indicators.note: From the South says the hidden letters are read backwards
abridged says the words are cut short so that only a run of their letters inside them is used

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A quoted heading, then a remark that a shortened show was watched carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'abridged performance' is wrong: a matinee is not shortened, and the hidden word needs 'abridged' as its signal, leaving 'performance' as the definition. Read upwards ('From the South'), sEEN IT A Meticulously gives it.
explanation.definitionFit: A matinee is an afternoon showing of a play or film, one kind of theatrical show.

clue.text: Man perhaps grabbed by boss and taken for a ride

indicators.note: grabbed by puts the island inside the letters for the boss

parts.note: MD is managing director, a boss
the Isle of Man is an example of an isle

explanation.surface: A fellow seized by his employer and swindled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a man; it is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To be taken for a ride is to be deceived or conned, the idiom for being led astray.

clue.text: Wife has desire to make magic

parts.note: an itch is a restless desire
to craft is to make by hand

explanation.surface: A wife longs to perform sorcery.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the practice of sorcery and spells, a synonym for enchantment.

clue.text: Crown holding the setter to account

indicators.note: to means the setter is added on after the account

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: A monarch's crown is linked to holding the compiler responsible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' is a link here: the crown holds, i.e. is, the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown of something is its top or peak, the highest point reached.

clue.text: Main track's out of the way

definitions.meaning: the principal song on a single record, the lead side of a disc
set apart or to one side

explanation.surface: A main railway line is away from it all.
explanation.definitionFit: On a record the lead song is on side A; as one word it means off to the side.

clue.text: She's into 20, darling, let loose without Romeo!

indicators.note: let loose means the remaining letters run free into a new order
without says the letter for Romeo is removed from darling

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A sweetheart loves witchcraft and runs wild once her Romeo is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is WITCHCRAFT; Glinda is the Good Witch of the North in The Wizard of Oz.
explanation.definitionFit: Glinda is the good sorceress of Oz, so she is a woman devoted to spells.

clue.text: Sun's first with press club

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of Sun's

parts.note: and means with, joining things together
to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: The Sun newspaper leads the way with a press club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press club' looks like a journalists' club; the club is a golf club for bunkers.
explanation.definitionFit: This lofted golf club is used to play out of bunkers, so it is one of a golfer's clubs.

clue.text: Delivery in Underwood's last over also turning, short of length — runs added

indicators.note: last takes the final letter of Underwood's

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: added means the runs letter is put in among the remaining letters
short of means the letter for length is missing
turning means the word also is read backwards

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket ball bowled by Derek Underwood that spins, falls short and concedes runs.
explanation.walkthrough: Derek Underwood was an England spin bowler. 'turning' makes OSLA from ALSO; 'short of' L leaves OSA, and R is 'added' inside to give OSRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A doosra is a ball from an off-spinner that turns the opposite way, a type of cricket bowl.

clue.text: Take out daughter — excellent lunch except the enchiladas for starters

indicators.note: for starters takes the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Someone takes their daughter out for a superb meal, skipping the Mexican dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take out' looks like a lunch invitation; it means remove or erase.
explanation.definitionFit: To delete is to remove or strike out text, a synonym for removing.
